fix(frontend): show a changed cover on the item page straight away (#762)

## What and why

Fixes #762

After changing an item's cover from the Files gallery, the cover photo at the top of the item page kept showing the old picture until the page was reloaded. The gallery reloaded its own list but never told the page, and the header cover is only refreshed by the empty-cover placeholder's upload.

- `MediaGallery` takes a new `oncoverchange` callback, called after the cover is set, removed or deleted, and after an upload that becomes the cover.
- The item page reads just the header cover again when told, with its own refresh key, so the gallery is not remounted and keeps its place.
- Setting a cover now swaps the picture above; removing it brings back the type's placeholder.

## Testing notes

- A new e2e spec, `cover-change.spec.ts`, failed before the change and passes after: setting a cover from the gallery changes the picture above without a reload, and removing it brings back the placeholder.
- The existing cover placeholder, swap and loading specs still pass.
- Frontend: unit tests, typecheck and lint pass.

Screenshot, after setting the second picture as the cover (the header shows it, with no reload):

![Cover changed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7456f9eb-57a1-421a-932b-b27f25ea30cc)

## Checks

- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (prek runs the `poe check` hooks on every commit; run `poe check` yourself if you skipped them)
- [ ] `poe coverage` passes (backend changes)
- [x] Tests added or updated for the change
- [x] Docs updated where behaviour, configuration or the data model changed
- [x] One focused change
- [ ] Breaking change (existing behaviour, API or data changes): the `breaking-change` label is applied

benchmarks.task_description:
Keep speed management from slowing a leg to 0 knots

Speed management no longer slows a sailing condition to 0 knots or below. Where the propulsion load sets no minimum speed above 0 (a float, Variable or expression load, or a table from 0 kn without a `MinimumLoad` that keeps the speed above 0), no condition sails below the route's lowest reference speed. Decks whose load sets a positive minimum, every library deck among them, do not move.

## Why

Speed management sets each condition's speed to the searched mean plus the condition's offset, clipped to per-condition limits from the propulsion load. The lower limit could be 0 kn (a table starting at 0 kn) or −inf (a non-table load). A leg clipped to 0 kn or below takes no sea time, miles or energy, because `_calculate_trip` divides with `divide_nonzero`, so leaving the leg out was cheaper than sailing it, and the search settled there. With a `MaximumSpeedChange`, the mean crept towards that optimum, the leg's sea time grew without bound just above 0 kn, and the bunkering LP became infeasible.

`calculate_speed_limits` (renamed from `calculate_technical_speed_limits`, since its minimum is no longer only technical) now replaces any minimum that is not above 0 with the lowest reference speed of the conditions the route sails, capped at the condition's maximum. Any positive minimum keeps the leg in the trip, and its cost then rises as the speed falls, so the search no longer has a cheap discontinuity to settle on.

Addresses #972

## Decisions

- The stand-in minimum is the route's lowest sailed reference speed, not a small constant: it comes from the deck, route speeds are positive by validation, and it is the same route envelope `calculate_mean_speed_bounds` already falls back on for the mean speed of a non-table load.
- The maximum side is unchanged: a non-table load still has no upper limit, so a fast condition may still exceed the route's highest speed. That produces no invalid result, and capping it would move results the issue does not ask to move.
- Where the power capacity caps the maximum below the route's lowest speed, the stand-in minimum is that maximum, so the reported limits stay ordered and the vessel sails at the cap; before, such a deck could slow below it towards 0 kn.
- No input validation was added: a load table starting at 0 kn and `MinimumLoad = 0` stay legitimate inputs.
- `_verify_vessel_speed_limits` reads the technical limits directly, since it checks what the propulsion converter can do.

## Results

Only decks with speed management, a propulsion load that sets no minimum speed above 0, and route speeds that differ between conditions move. The issue's reproduction (`example_1` with feeder speed management, route speeds 19 / 19 / 5 kn), `feeder_oil` in 2027:

| Deck | Search bounds (kn) | Speeds per leg (kn) | Ballast sea days/year |
|---|---|---|---|
| Table from 0 kn, `MinimumLoad = 0`, before | 0.00–19.50 | 11.50, 11.50, 0.00 | 0.0 |
| Table from 0 kn, `MinimumLoad = 0`, after | 5.00–19.50 | 11.50, 11.50, 5.00 | 45.0 |
| Expression load, before | 5.00–19.00 | 10.07, 10.07, −3.93 | 0.0 |
| Expression load, after | 5.00–19.00 | 10.07, 10.07, 5.00 | 42.8 |

The ballast leg is now sailed at the route's lowest speed instead of being left out. With `MaximumSpeedChange = 0.5` the first deck runs to completion instead of stopping in 2036 with an infeasible bunkering error. `minimum_speed` and `lowest_speed` for such vessels now report the route's lowest speed, where a non-table load reported −inf and a negative speed before.

## Limitations

- `maximum_speed` still reports inf for a vessel with a non-table propulsion load under speed management, as before.
- Proposed test (`tests/end_to_end/`, behaviour): the issue's expression-load deck, asserting that every `vessel.lowest_speed` of the feeders is at least the route's lowest reference speed, 5 kn; the oracle is the route's own speeds in the deck.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix: review an allowlisted bot's PR even without a requester marker

## Why
De-Kalo/dbarnacle#1242 got no review. A PR opened by a `requester_delegating_bots` bot is dropped as a bot event unless its body carries the `imparity-requested-by` marker. dBarnacle leaves the marker out whenever it can't resolve the requester's GitHub account, which is true for nearly all its recent PRs, so they were silently skipped.

## What
- An allowlisted bot opening its own PR now passes the bot filter whether or not the body has a marker.
  - With a marker: reviewed on the requester's own tokens, as before.
  - Without one: reviewed on the regular model chain.
- Other events from the bot (`ready_for_review`, `synchronize`, a different sender id, a non-allowlisted bot) stay ignored.
- I moved the "allowlisted bot opened its own PR" check into a helper, `_delegating_bot_opened_own_pr`, so the gate and `_requester_identity` use the same rule.
- Added a comment to `configuration.toml` and regenerated the configuration reference.

The marker itself is being fixed separately: Imparity will store each member's GitHub login and send it with tasks, and dBarnacle will pass it through.

## Tests
`PYTHONPATH=. uv run pytest tests/unittest -q`: all pass. New cases cover a marker-less bot open (reviewed by the default agent) and other marker-less bot events (still ignored).
